[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
No goal-specific experiences were retrieved. The process lessons converge on verifying action preconditions before acting and not overgeneralizing from a single failure. Specifically: (1) Before moving toward a target, check the intended path for obstacles such as stools; if blocked, adjust the route or clear the obstacle rather than assuming forward movement will work. (2) A movement obstruction does not prove the target is unreachable; check the target's actual proximity and interaction range before predicting pickup failure. (3) Before attempting to pick an object, verify the robot's hand is empty; if it is holding something, place or drop that object first. (4) If a Find action fails, do not assume the target is present or visible; explore alternate locations or confirm object availability before relying on discovery.

## Preliminary Thinking
For a fetch-and-pick or put-away task, proceed as follows: 1. Discover the target with Find; if Find fails, search alternate locations and confirm the object's availability rather than assuming it is visible. 2. Before navigating, inspect the path for obstacles; if blocked, plan a clear route or clear the obstacle instead of assuming a direct move will succeed. 3. Move toward the target; if movement fails, do not conclude the object is unreachable. Check actual proximity and interaction range. 4. Before Pick, ensure the hand is empty; if not, place or drop the held object first. 5. Attempt Pick only when the target is within reach, then complete the remainder of the task (e.g., carry the potato to the cooking area or place each object in its designated location).
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
